name: password-field
description: Password field for sign-in and sign-up. Sign-in: show/hide that hides itself again, autofill, IME chain, felt errors. Sign-up: rules tick live under the field with a strength word, so nobody learns the rules from an error.
avoidWhen: Do not use for one-time codes; use otp-input. Do not set isError per keystroke; on sign-up pass rules instead and validate on submit.

ux.behaviour: On sign-up, each rule under the field flips to a filled check the moment it is met, with a tick haptic; all met fires confirm and the strength word reads Strong
ux.why: You watch the password become acceptable instead of guessing and being told no
ux.reducedMotion: Marks flip without the crossfade; haptics unchanged

ux.behaviour: Strength is a word (Weak, Good, Strong) with ink segments, never colour alone; it appears once there is something to judge
ux.why: A bar with no words is a guess; a red bar on an empty field is a scold

ux.behaviour: The eye crossfades between show and hide; a revealed password hides again when focus leaves the field and after 10 seconds without typing
ux.why: You peek to check a character, not to leave it on screen for the next person
ux.reducedMotion: Icon swaps without the crossfade; the timers are unchanged

ux.behaviour: A paste or autofill is trimmed of surrounding whitespace; typed spaces are kept
ux.why: Password managers add a stray newline; the field should not make you find it

ux.behaviour: On the error edge the field shakes once, fires reject, and the message shows on the field (inherited from text-field)
ux.why: The refusal is felt before it is read
ux.reducedMotion: No shake; haptic and text only

ux.behaviour: The first keystroke after an error drops the error colour and keeps the message quiet until blur (inherited from text-field)
With a hardware keyboard, the hint line says Caps lock is on while the field is focused
ux.why: Most wrong passwords on a keyboard are the right password in the wrong case

ux.behaviour: IME Done clears focus (hiding any reveal); Next moves to the next field; a reveal survives rotation but the idle timer restarts
ux.why: Leaving the field is the moment to put the password away

aiHints: Sign-up: pass rules (PasswordRule.minLength, number, upperCase, ...) and ContentType.NewPassword; do not also flag isError while typing
Sign-in: no rules; set isError with supportingText on a rejected submit, and flip it off before setting it again for a second rejection
When isError is true, pass supportingText; color-only errors are rejected
The reveal hides on its own; do not add a timer or a blur handler in the caller
Rule labels are plain strings so they can come from resources; keep them short, they wrap at 2x font
